# Importing into analysis

Everything we described with `FrDj` can become actual rizin analysis
objects: classes, methods and struct types.

## 1. Import one class

```text
[0x00000000]> Froj frida://attach/usb//FridaMin
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":2812,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}

[0x00000000]> FrImj re.frida.minapp.secret.SecretVault
{"ok":true,"result":{"imported":true,"class":"re.frida.minapp.secret.SecretVault","loader":0,"methods":4,"constructors":1,"fields":1}}
```

The class, its methods, constructors and fields are now in rizin analysis.

## 2. Verify

```text
[0x00000000]> acl
[re_frida_minapp_secret_SecretVault]
```

```text
[0x00000000]> ts
...
re_frida_minapp_secret_SecretVault
```

```text
[0x00000000]> tcd re_frida_minapp_secret_SecretVault
struct re_frida_minapp_secret_SecretVault { char *SECRET_B64; };
```

![Import verification](img/android_journey/import-verify.png)

The Java field `String SECRET_B64` became a C struct member `char *SECRET_B64`.
The mapping:

| Java | C |
|---|---|
| `int` | `int` |
| `long` | `long long` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `double` | `double` |
| `float` | `float` |
| `byte` | `int8_t` |
| `short` | `int16_t` |
| `char` | `uint16_t` |
| `java.lang.String` | `char *` |
| anything else | `void *` |

## 3. Synthetic and primitive fields

Inner classes carry a synthetic `this$0` field, and primitive fields map
to C types. Import a listener:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrImj re.frida.minapp.MainActivity$6
{"ok":true,"result":{"imported":true,"class":"re.frida.minapp.MainActivity$6","loader":0,"methods":1,"constructors":1,"fields":2}}

[0x00000000]> tcd re_frida_minapp_MainActivity_6
struct re_frida_minapp_MainActivity_6 { void *this_0; long long lastActionAt; };
```

Dots and `$` become underscores in type names. The synthetic field is
sanitized to `this_0`, and the Java `long` field became C `long long`.

## 4. Batch import

A class name **without a dot** is a prefix: every loaded class starting with
it is imported, capped by `frida.java.max`:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrImj re
{"ok":true,"result":{"batch":true,"classes":21,"methods":85,"fields":34,"constructors":25}}
```

```text
[0x00000000]> acl
[re_frida_minapp_Calculator]
[re_frida_minapp_MainActivity]
[re_frida_minapp_NativeLib]
[re_frida_minapp_secret_SecretVault]
...
```

A prefix with no matches is an error:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrImj com.unknown
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_target","message":"no matching classes found for the given prefix"}}
```

## 5. Re-importing a class

Re-importing an existing class does not crash and does not duplicate state:

```text
[0x00000000]> FrImj re.frida.minapp.secret.SecretVault
{"ok":true,"result":{"imported":true,"class":"re.frida.minapp.secret.SecretVault","loader":0,"methods":4,"constructors":1,"fields":1}}
```

## 6. Runtime module flags

`Frfj` imports every loaded module as a flag in the `frida.libs` space,
named after the module at its base address:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frfj
{"ok":true,"result":{"imported":true,"modules":322}}

[0x00000000]> fs frida.libs
[0x00000000]> fl~libnative
0x7adfac850000 20480 libnative.so
```

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[agent: classDescribe] --> B[host: rz_analysis_class_create]
    B --> C[rz_analysis_class_method_set]
    B --> D[rz_analysis_class_base_set]
    B --> E[fields into the type database]
    E --> F[ts / tcd struct types]
    C --> G[ac / acl classes]
```

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Import `GameState`, batch-import `re.frida`, verify with `acl` and `ts`,
then import the runtime modules with `Frfj` and grep the flags.
:::
